clue.text: Someone always ready for action General Tom Thumb, perhaps

definitions.meaning: an American colonial militiaman pledged to turn out at a moment's notice
the famously tiny showman of P T Barnum's circus was literally a very small man

explanation.surface: A clue praising a soldier always on standby, who turns out to be a circus midget general.
explanation.walkthrough: General Tom Thumb was the stage name of Charles Stratton, a tiny performer in Barnum's shows; read the answer as MINUTE (tiny) MAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Militiamen of the American Revolution were named for being ready to fight within a minute; the second sense is a tiny person.

clue.text: Great coat worn by soldier

indicators.note: the soldier is wrapped inside the coat as if wearing it

parts.note: a mac is a mackintosh raincoat
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier dons a fine greatcoat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Great coat' tempts as one word, greatcoat; 'Great' is the definition and 'coat' gives MAC.
explanation.definitionFit: Magic is informal British slang for excellent, so it can stand for great as an exclamation of approval.

clue.text: Bill and coo, side by side

parts.note: to bill is to kiss and caress, which is also to neck
taken as written
to coo as lovers do is to murmur fondly while necking

explanation.surface: Lovebirds bill and coo, sitting side by side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill and coo' is a phrase for courting; each verb gives the slang NECK.
explanation.definitionFit: Racers neck and neck are level with each other, running side by side.

clue.text: Nanki-Poo, for instance, established church out east on line

indicators.note: the letter for east is moved out to the eastern, right-hand end

parts.note: a minster is a large church established by a monastery

explanation.surface: An opera character is set up in a church out east, in a row.
explanation.walkthrough: Nanki-Poo, the hero of Gilbert and Sullivan's The Mikado, sings 'A wandering minstrel I'; MINSTER with its E sent to the end gives MINSTRE.
explanation.definitionFit: In The Mikado the hero disguises himself as a travelling musician, an example of the role.

clue.text: Jewel container turned up in tree

indicators.note: in a down clue turned up means the pieces are read from bottom to top

parts.note: a gem is a jewel
a tun is a large cask

explanation.surface: A jewel box is found upturned in a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses the whole run GEMTUN.
explanation.definitionFit: The nutmeg is an evergreen tropical tree whose seed gives the spice.

clue.text: Naval officer gets Italian to come clean

parts.note: Adm is the abbreviation for admiral
It is a standard abbreviation for Italian (as in gin and It)

explanation.surface: A naval commander persuades an Italian to confess.
explanation.definitionFit: To come clean is to confess, a common idiom for owning up to the truth.

clue.text: Clothing to provoke outrage when worn by relative outsiders

indicators.note: worn by places the outside letters within the verb, as if it wears them

parts.note: to appal is to shock and outrage

indicators.note: outsiders are the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A garment is so shocking that the in-laws are appalled when they wear it.
explanation.walkthrough: The outsiders of 'relative', R and E, go inside APPAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparel is a formal word for clothes and garments.

clue.text: Clean hair

definitions.meaning: to clean a floor with a wet swab
a thick untidy head of hair

explanation.definitionFit: A mop is a floor-cleaning tool, and also a shaggy mass of hair.

clue.text: Plant used to cure people suffering endless harm

parts.note: torment is severe suffering

indicators.note: endless means the final letter is cut off

parts.note: ill as a noun means harm, as in to wish someone ill

explanation.surface: A herbal remedy is used to cure sufferers of chronic ailments.
explanation.walkthrough: ILL as a noun means harm; 'endless' cuts it to IL.
explanation.definitionFit: Tormentil is a small yellow-flowered herb whose root was used in folk medicine.

clue.text: Lizard for instance repelled by cold floor

indicators.note: something repelled is driven back, so the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: e.g. is short for exempli gratia, for instance
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
to floor an opponent is to knock them out, KO

explanation.surface: A lizard, perhaps, is put off by a chilly floor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for instance' looks like part of the definition but supplies EG, turned to GE by 'repelled'.
explanation.definitionFit: Geckos are small climbing lizards found in warm countries, an example of the reptile family.

clue.text: A pet prone to wander — it might carry a message

indicators.note: to wander is to stray about, so the letters of the three words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pet inclined to roam might be sent off with a message, like a carrier pigeon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'prone' reads as part of the description of the pet but is part of the fodder; 'wander' rearranges A PET PRONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Writing paper is what a letter is written on, so it literally carries a message.

clue.text: Bell showing time to tuck into pudding — British one

parts.note: a charlotte is a baked fruit pudding in a bread or sponge case

indicators.note: the time abbreviation is tucked inside the word one

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone rings a bell when it is time to eat pudding, the British way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bell' looks like a ringing thing; it is Currer Bell, the pen name under which the Jane Eyre author first published.
explanation.definitionFit: The novelist first published under the male pseudonym Currer Bell, so the pen name stands for the writer herself.

clue.text: In the Newcastle area, clay's black and blue

indicators.note: in places the soil and dark words inside the regional abbreviation

parts.note: NE is the North East of England, where Newcastle lies
clay is earth
ebon is a poetic word for black

explanation.surface: In Tyneside the clay is bruised black and blue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'black and blue' looks like bruising; 'blue' alone is the definition, meaning risqué.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue jokes are indecent, and near the bone means verging on the indecent or offensive.

clue.text: Difficult to understand returning to gallery, but good luck

parts.note: the gods is the highest gallery in a theatre

indicators.note: returning means the word for profound is read backwards

parts.note: deep thoughts are profound and hard to follow

explanation.surface: A theatregoer gives up on a baffling play and heads back to the upper gallery, wishing everyone luck.
explanation.walkthrough: The gods is the theatre's top gallery; DEEP turned by 'returning' gives PEED.
explanation.definitionFit: Godspeed is an old wish for success to someone setting off, much like saying good luck.

clue.text: Swaps — two I ought to pass up

indicators.note: swaps means the letters change places to make a new order

explanation.surface: A trader decides two deals he ought to refuse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swaps' rearranges TWO I OUGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: To go without something is to do without it, forgoing or passing it up.

clue.text: Accommodating one in factory

indicators.note: the numeral is placed inside the word for a works

parts.note: a plant is an industrial works or factory
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A single worker in a factory is obliging.
explanation.definitionFit: A pliant person bends easily to others' wishes, so is flexible and accommodating.

clue.text: Dog on the line it's mine

parts.note: a collie is a sheepdog
Ry is short for railway, a line

explanation.surface: A dog on the railway track claims it as its own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mine' looks possessive but means a coal pit.
explanation.definitionFit: A colliery is a coal mine with its buildings.

clue.text: You and I encounter black beetle

parts.note: the speaker and the person addressed together make we
black in the sense of wicked, as in black-hearted, means evil

explanation.surface: Two people come across a dark-coloured beetle.
explanation.definitionFit: Weevils are small snouted beetles that infest grain and other stored food.

clue.text: Within it I always include a shortened version of my name

definitions.text: a shortened version of my name

indicators.note: include signals the answer is contained within the run of words

explanation.surface: Someone always writes a short form of their name inside a document.
explanation.walkthrough: The run spans 'withIN IT I ALways'.
explanation.definitionFit: An initial is the first letter of a name, used as an abbreviation of it.

clue.text: Where you might find pal I shot, injured

definitions.text: Where you might find pal I shot, injured

indicators.note: injured letters are damaged and put back in a new order

explanation.surface: A remorseful shooter wonders where to find the friend he wounded.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: a wounded friend would be found in a ward, and 'injured' rearranges PAL I SHOT.
explanation.definitionFit: A wounded person is taken to the place where the sick and injured are treated.

clue.text: Table recently found in French city

indicators.note: found in places the word for recently inside the city name

parts.note: Pau is a city in south-west France
late means recently, as in of late

explanation.surface: A table was recently discovered in a French city.
explanation.definitionFit: A plateau is a tableland, a raised area of level ground.

clue.text: Turn singer into a bareback rider

parts.note: a go is a turn, as in it's your go
a diva is a leading opera singer

explanation.surface: A soprano is transformed into a circus horse rider.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bareback' is a pun: Lady Godiva rode naked through Coventry, bare of back as well as of saddle.
explanation.definitionFit: Legend says Lady Godiva rode through Coventry naked, so a horse rider with a bare back.

clue.text: Clear choice for one tempted to thieve — no more concessions

definitions.text: Clear choice for one tempted to thieve
definitions.meaning: a would-be thief faces the plain option of stealing the item or not
a final offer, with no further bargaining allowed

explanation.surface: A shoplifter's dilemma becomes a hard-nosed negotiator's final offer.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is literal: steal the thing or walk away from it.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is said when an offer is final and there will be no further haggling or compromise.

clue.text: Plant pronouns together

parts.note: thy is an archaic possessive pronoun
me is the object form of I

explanation.surface: A gardener puts a pair of pronouns side by side to name a herb.
explanation.definitionFit: Thyme is an aromatic herb used in cooking.

clue.text: In deep water? Not if you keep your footing

definitions.text: In deep water? Not if you keep your footing

parts.words: In deep water? Not if you keep your footing
parts.note: a figurative phrase for being in a risky position, read literally as standing on a frozen surface that might crack

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a person in trouble could keep steady footing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In deep water' is the idiom for trouble; the follow-up pictures a skater on a frozen pond who stays dry only if the surface holds.
explanation.definitionFit: Being in a precarious position is figuratively being in deep water, at risk of falling through.

clue.text: Toddler starts to trip over things

indicators.note: starts to means the first letter of each following word is taken; the same letters also running across 'to trip' is a coincidence

explanation.surface: A small child begins to stumble over things.
explanation.definitionFit: A tot is a small child, a toddler.

clue.text: Last to use unpleasant resin

indicators.note: the final letter of the word use is taken

parts.note: poxy is British slang for nasty or worthless

explanation.surface: Instructions say to apply an unpleasant resin last.
explanation.walkthrough: POXY is informal British slang for rotten or second-rate.
explanation.definitionFit: Epoxy is a synthetic resin used as a strong adhesive or coating.

clue.text: Drink everything? Not quite everything

parts.note: a tot is a small measure of spirits

indicators.note: not quite means falling short by a letter, so the last is dropped

parts.note: everything is all

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether to drink the lot, and is told not quite all of it.
explanation.definitionFit: Total as a noun means the whole amount, the complete sum of things.

clue.text: See our way diverted back to square one (2,3,4) 22,907 Soluti

indicators.note: a diverted route takes a different course, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A traveller finds the road diverted and ends up back where they started.
explanation.definitionFit: The military command restores the previous position, just as going back to square one returns to a starting point.
